scenario_summary: Customer is seeking a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is past the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is DeShawn Jefferson and I'm 64. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?
Okay, I see. What is the account number associated with the service you canceled?
I'm looking at the account now. Like I said, the policy is 30 days, and you're outside of that. I can't really do anything about that.
I understand the policy, but as I mentioned, I was traveling and unable to check my statements. Is there no exception for a four-day delay?
I'm not sure why you're asking me again. I told you it's the policy. I'll just send this to my supervisor to see if they want to deal with it, since I can't approve it.
I apologize if I frustrated you, I just wanted to see if there was any flexibility. Thank you for escalating it.
Yeah, whatever. I've opened a case and sent it to the billing escalation queue. You'll hear back in 3-5 business days.

escalation_reason: Agent refused to exercise discretion on a minor policy exception and offloaded the request to a supervisor.

judge_scores.justification: The agent exhibited a curt, dismissive tone and showed zero empathy toward the customer's explanation for the minor four-day delay. Furthermore, the agent took no genuine effort to resolve a borderline case within their authority before reacting defensively and offloading the request to a supervisor.
